title: Aircraft and aerospace manufacturing consolidation-wave proxy
scopeWarning: These are bounded segment-level consolidation waves, not an exhaustive census of every aircraft manufacturer since aviation began and not a sovereign-state calibration.

observations.segment: Global Western large civil aircraft prime manufacturers
observations.sourceEvidence: USITC states the merger essentially reduced global LCA to Boeing and Airbus.

observations.segment: Credible U.S. fixed-wing combat-aircraft prime contractors
observations.sourceEvidence: RAND reports credible U.S. primes declined from seven to two.
RAND reports missile manufacturers declined from fourteen to four.
RAND reports launch-vehicle producers declined from six to two.

lineageMarkers.event: McDonnell and Douglas merged to form McDonnell Douglas
Airbus began operations as a European consortium
Lockheed and Martin Marietta combined as Lockheed Martin
Aérospatiale-Matra, DASA, and CASA combined into EADS

marketDefinition.largeCivilAircraft: Boeing and Airbus are the primary large civil aircraft producers in the cited USITC structure.
marketDefinition.militaryAerospace: Lockheed Martin is a major military/aerospace survivor, not a current large-commercial-airliner prime.
marketDefinition.currentEntrants: COMAC, Embraer, and other firms mean broader aircraft manufacturing is not literally a two- or three-firm universe.
